study type: Retrospective analysis of a nationally representative survey
exposure: Women who did not have doula support
Women who desired but did not have doula support
cohort: Women who delivered a singleton baby in a US hospital in 2011-2012 (N = 2400)
finding: Women with doula support had lower odds of both cesarean delivery and nonindicated cesarean delivery compared to women who did not have a doula and those who desired but did not have doula support.
mod_finding: Doula-supported women had lower odds of cesarean compared without doula support and those who desired but did not have doula support (AOR = 0.41, CI, 0.18-0.96; and AOR = 0.31, CI, 0.13-0.74).
